title: Review of c08's NRCH swimmers (SIM): replicates on fresh seed 5 and at dt/2; swimmers are crowded and churn through merges
summary: Fresh seed 5 (192^2, T=6000, the author's command): the uniform noisy state nucleates droplets at t~1300 that turn into polar crescents with a psi crest on one side and swim; 10 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, the best 12.6 body lengths at speed 0.16 (net/path 0.96). The same seed at dt=0.025 (labkit labels time at the META dt, so its times are 2x and speeds 1/2 the true ones) gives 9 such tracks, the best 20.4 body lengths at true speed ~0.19, with crescents that keep their polar shape for thousands of time units (rerun_dt2/seed5/tracks.png #35, #42). The population is dense and collisional: merge/split 1.17 at dt and 0.71 at dt/2, longest track 58 and 84 of 121 frames.

observations.S: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=0-1050: uniform field with weak noise; droplets appear at t=1300
observations.I: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=1300-6000: discrete droplets of similar size; lifetimes between collisions (thousands of t) far exceed formation (~200 t)
observations.M: rerun/seed5 FACTS: 10 tracks >= 1 body length, track 43 12.6 body lengths, net/path 0.96; rerun_dt2/seed5: track #35 a polar crescent over the whole crop strip, best 20.4 body lengths

not_checked: the reciprocal and sub-threshold twins (author's pack_recip, pack_sub)
verdicts.limitation: A literature result (Brauns & Marchetti 2024). The droplets are crowded: they collide, merge and break up (merge/split 0.7-1.2), so identity persists only between collisions and shape varies with them; no reproduction. I did not re-run the nonreciprocity controls.
